理或倍經訓而好自用或泥故常而不知變眩於
裁擇失其關鍵求以活人而殺人者多矣我

宣宗大王以理身之法推濟衆之仁留心醫學軫念民

朝鮮總督府圖書之印

貢737
translation:
[Title character: Yi (易 / Change)]

From Qi Bo and Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor] above, exhausting the heavenly principles, and below, penetrating the patterns of human affairs — it would be unsuitable to be dismissive. The writings that emerged and became known were difficult [to master]; after the methods were corrupted, later generations had physicians who possessed books. From that point down to the present, schools and lineages proliferated, books on medicine multiplied, and the two arts [medicine and pharmacy] became ever more obscure in their essentials. Various masters — Liu, Zhang, Zhu, Li, and a hundred schools — arose one after another, and their theories diverged widely from the Lingshu and the original teachings, with few points of agreement. The mediocre physicians of the age, unable to fathom the depths, either went against the classical teachings and liked to act on their own authority, or clung to old conventions and knew not how to adapt, becoming confused in their selection and losing the essential keys. Many who sought to save lives ended up taking lives instead.

Our King Seonjo [Seonrong the Great King], applying the methods of cultivating his own person and extending to the benevolence of relieving the people, turned his heart toward the study of medicine and gave deep thought to the welfare of the people.

[Stamp: Seal of the Library of the Government-General of Joseon]

text:
召太醫臣許浚

敎曰近見中朝方書皆是抄集庸瑣不足觀兩宜裒聚諸方輯成一書且人之疾病皆生於不善調養為先藥石次之諸方浩繁務擇其要窮村巷無醫藥而人不能知爾宜分而天折者多我國鄉藥多產而儒醫鄭碏太醫楊頗並書鄉名使民易知淺退與

禮壽金應鐸李命源鄭禮男等設局撰集略成肯

紫值丁酉之亂諸醫星散事遂寢嚴後

先王又敎許浚獨為撰成仍出內藏方書五百卷以資
translation:
Summoning the Royal Physician, subject Heo Jun:

The King's instruction read: "Having lately perused the medical books from China, I find them all to be mere compilations of mediocre and trivial material, not worthy of regard. It is fitting to gather and compile the various prescriptions into a single work. Moreover, human illness arises first from poor care of oneself, with medicines and remedies coming second. The prescriptions are vast in number; select only the essential ones. In remote villages and alleys where there are no physicians or medicines, people cannot know what to do, so you should distinguish and clarify. The many premature deaths stem from this. Our country's native medicinal herbs are abundantly produced, and the scholar-physician Jeong Jak and the royal physician Yang [name] should write alongside the local names of herbs so that the common people may easily recognize them." [The King] had [Heo Jun] collaborate with [officials including] Je Su, Kim Eung-tak, Yi Myeong-won, Jeong Ye-nam and others to establish an office and compile [the work], and it was nearly complete—

But then the Jeong-yu War [the Japanese invasions of 1597] broke out, the physicians scattered, and the project came to a halt.

The late King then further instructed Heo Jun to compile the work alone, and provided him with five hundred volumes of books from the Royal Library as resources.

龍駒賓天至
考據撰未半而
聖上即位之三年庚戌浚始卒業而投
進目之曰東醫寶鑑書凡二十五卷
上覽而嘉之下敎曰陽平君許浚曾在
先朝特承撰集醫方之
命積年單忠至於覽論流離之中不廢其功乃編帙
以進之仍令
先王命撰之書告成於寡眛嗣服之後子不勝悲感其
賜後太僕馬一匹以酬其勞浚令內醫院設廳鋟
translation:
While the compilation was not yet half finished, the Dragon Steed ascended to heaven [i.e., the king passed away].

In the third year of His Majesty's reign, the year Gyeongsul [1610], Jun finally completed the work and submitted it, titling it Dongui Bogam, comprising a total of twenty-five volumes.

His Majesty reviewed it and, pleased, issued a royal decree saying: "Yang-pyeong-gun Heo Jun, who had previously served under the former court and received the special royal command to compile and assemble medical formularies, toiled single-mindedly over many years, and even amid wandering and hardship did not abandon his work but completed the compilation and presented it.

That the book commanded to be compiled by the Former King has been completed and presented to Us in Our unworthy succession — We cannot help but feel deep sorrow and gratitude. Accordingly, he is granted one horse from the Office of the Royal Stables as recompense for his labors."

Jun then directed the Inner Medical Office to establish a hall and engrave [the text for printing].

命提調臣延龜撰序文弁之卷首曰竊念太和一散六氣不調癘殘扎癘迭為民災則為醫藥以濟其大死是宗帝王仁政務焉術非書則不載書非擇則不精擇不博則理不明傳不廣則不惠布是書也該括古今折衷群言探本窮源掣綱提要詳而不至於蔓約而無所不包始自內景外形分為難病諸方以至脈訣症論藥性治法攝養要義鍼石諸規靡不單具并不茂即病者雖千百其佐而補瀉緩急泛應曲當蓋不必遠稽古籍近

6
translation:
Printed and distributed widely, both within and beyond [the country].

I was commanded to serve as Director and compose a preface to head the volumes. It reads: I humbly reflect that when the harmony of the primal force disperses and the six vital energies fall out of balance, pestilence and plague repeatedly become disasters for the people; thus medicine exists to bring relief. The great task of preserving life is what the benevolent governance of sage kings and emperors attends to. What is not recorded in books cannot be transmitted; books that lack selection lack refinement; selection without breadth leaves principles obscure; transmission without wide reach fails to bring benefit. This book is comprehensive, encompassing all that is ancient and modern, striking a balance among many views, tracing matters to their roots and exhausting their sources, drawing together the essential threads and highlighting the key points. It is thorough without becoming diffuse, concise yet leaving nothing out. Beginning with the Inner Landscape and Outer Form, it is divided into sections covering various diseases and prescriptions, and extending to pulse diagnosis, symptom discussion, the nature of medicines, treatment methods, cultivation and nourishment essentials, and the rules for acupuncture and stone needles — nothing is omitted or cursorily treated. Even if a practitioner faces hundreds or thousands of patients, and must supplement or drain, relax or urgently respond — adapting to all circumstances and hitting the mark in each case — there is no need to consult distant ancient texts or recent...

translation:
This compilation sets out [medical formulas] organized by category, so that upon seeing [symptoms], one may find the matching remedy and administer the appropriate treatment as surely as a tally-stick matches its counterpart. It is truly a precious mirror for physicians and a fine method for benefiting the world. All of this originates from the marvelous plans transmitted by the former kings, and embodies our
Holy Majesty's continued and expansive intention — reflecting the virtue of benevolence toward the people and love for all things, and the way of making practical use of resources for the enrichment of life.
In both its earlier and later parts, the work is of one consistent principle: that the governance of bringing harmony and nurturing all within the realm lies precisely herein. As the saying goes, "A benevolent person's exercise of mind — how far-reaching its benefits are!" Can one doubt that this is so?

東醫寶鑑內景篇卷之一

御醫忠勤貞亮扈聖功臣崇祿大夫陽平君臣許浚奉　教撰

集例

臣謹按以成人身內有五臟六府又外有筋骨肌肉之血脈百體之內經之主道家之三要釋氏之四大境皆謂此也黃庭以清靜內府精氣神藏得家治是道府為其內精藏篇五六次得修備篇為五連

飲板外法面三頭今此飲肉景精氣治

湯液針灸其境之卷諸病之證外篇又採

突重

古人藥方動入之材兩太多辛難備用方醫學正一

刻之數尤多貧寒之家何以辦此得
translation:
Dongui Bogam (Treasured Mirror of Eastern Medicine), Internal Medicine Section, Volume One

Composed by royal physician Heo Jun, holder of the titles Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Bright, Merit Subject of護聖, Senior First Rank, Lord of Yangpyeong, by royal command.

Editorial Notes

I, your servant, respectfully observe: the human body internally contains the five viscera and six bowels, and externally has sinews, bones, muscles, flesh, blood, and vessels throughout the hundred parts. The Inner Classic speaks of this as its governing principle; Taoist practitioners consider it the three essentials; Buddhist teachings call it the four great elements — all refer to this very thing. The Yellow Court [Classic] regards the interior organs of stillness and clarity, the essence, vital breath, and spirit as stored within; the household of the Tao is governed by nurturing and cultivating these stored essences, organizing them into sections and chapters.

The basis of [inner] landscape is taken as the foundation. Medical texts also contain inner and outer sections on essence and vital breath of the viscera and bowels, compiled and arranged into chapters.

Nourishing [the body] is the essential matter. This present work arranges methods for the limbs, joints, and muscles, the diagnosis of outer sections, and the essence and vital breath of the viscera, organized into further chapters.

Decoctions, acupuncture, and moxibustion — the volumes on these matters and the signs of the various diseases are treated in the outer sections.

[By reading] the auspicious and inauspicious, life and death, and recognizing their signs, one can see clearly. If a physician causes the patient to understand the pulse and opens the path of proper treatment, then the suffering of the desperate patient will be lightened.

In ancient prescriptions, the ingredients used were often many — both costly and acrid — and difficult to obtain. How could a poor family prepare all of these? The number [of such ingredients] is especially great, and for impoverished households it is very hard to provide for.

遊地以今東醫書寶鑑名之覧吉京古輕人之故遺明鑑意有存生齊桀竟武寶
translation:
The text discusses the tradition of medical prescriptions typically using five coins' weight as a standard measure, which has become overly rigid and formulaic, with prescriptions often containing only four or five ingredients or eight flavors.

It discusses the nature of seasonal medicinal properties — particularly around the Spring Equinox — and their subtle qualities, noting their ability to cut through illness, and references ancient physicians and their pharmacopeias.

The passage criticizes those who wish to study medicine without first understanding the foundational texts, referencing the Divine Husbandman's Materia Medica (Shennong Bencao), noting that the original herbal canon is vast and complex.

It discusses how formulas and medical knowledge were transmitted from regions such as Shaanxi and the west, and how Eastern medicine developed its own tradition.

It references the brilliance of illuminating all things, comparing it to how medicine reveals the true form of illness, and notes that during the Yuan dynasty, Eastern medicine began to develop its own identity.

The passage concludes by explaining the naming of the Dongui Bogam (東醫寶鑑 — Treasured Mirror of Eastern Medicine), stating that what has long been lightly regarded — the medical heritage of the East — is now preserved and illuminated for posterity, for the benefit of sustaining life.

孫真人曰天地之內以人為貴頭圓象天足方象地天有四時人有四肢天有五行人有五藏天有六極人有六腑天有九藪人有九竅天有十二時人有十二經脈天有二十四氣人有二十四俞天有三百六十五度人有三百六十五節天天有晝夜人有寤寐天有雷電人有喜怒天有雨露人有眼目天有陰陽人有寒熱地有泉水人有血脈地有草木人有毛髮地有金石人有齒牙此假合成形人有雷電熟地有寒熱合人有常假成形

人痿多瘦人丹火多白兀及之黑形懺肺氣虛黑者治法適別足

朱之淺色白兀不及之黑形長不及蒼短薄不及厚而肥不及

南人皆有禀四大五常假成牙

人有毛髮天地有金石人有齒牙

形人色斑殊藏府亦異外證雖同治法適別
translation:
Sun Simiao said: Within heaven and earth, humans are the most precious. The head is round, resembling heaven; the feet are square, resembling the earth. Heaven has four seasons, humans have four limbs. Heaven has five phases, humans have five viscera. Heaven has six poles, humans have six bowels. Heaven has nine marshes, humans have nine orifices. Heaven has twelve hours, humans have twelve meridians. Heaven has twenty-four solar terms, humans have twenty-four transport points. Heaven has three hundred sixty-five degrees, humans have three hundred sixty-five joints. Heaven has day and night, humans have waking and sleep. Heaven has thunder and lightning, humans have joy and anger. Heaven has rain and dew, humans have eyes. Heaven has yin and yang, humans have cold and heat. The earth has spring water, humans have blood vessels. The earth has plants and trees, humans have hair. The earth has metal and stone, humans have teeth. All these come together to form the human body.

Among people, some are thin and emaciated; some have a fiery constitution with a fair complexion, tending toward dark complexion; the lungs may be deficient; those with a dark complexion require different methods of treatment.

People of the south all receive the endowment of the four great elements and the five constants, forming the body.

Although the external manifestations may appear similar, the internal conditions differ, and the methods of treatment must be distinguished accordingly.

形氣之始
乾素靈太慶云天者未見氣也乾有太初者太始也太始也太初大始也太易氣之始也太初者始見氣也太始者始見形也太素者始見質也。形始者癥之始也病始者形之始也素問曰從太極混淪。易曰乾坤易有註曰太極是生兩儀具日從氣已具形而病從形生子具太易廣日混合之稠為鴻蒙具易而病太太太分乾太蒙而病太

极也未從太極混淪。易曰乾坤而太始之為乾坤者亦太類此初之之調變也混合之分為乾太

坤分之而始為惠方曰天精地之始也子乾天之合列乾坤者而太言極之生兩也廣日從易稠為鴻蒙具易而病太

魂曰形之始也太神之始乃化萬物其之二精

胎孕之始
月成筋骨成而六月相生三七月遊魂其魂四月能動女右分二精

五月成筋其果六月李以氣之始也子也類此初

八月子貧解四而十九。日而始于胎然後七日氣而一九憂日月

而不足者手八月子貧解其魂動左生三月者三而胞十段而胞一九有月滿右分

而陰陽大定解四而十九。日而始于胎然後七日氣而一九憂日月
translation:
Body Form

The Beginning of Form and Qi
The Qian (Heaven) element in the Su (Plain) and Ling (Spiritual) texts; the Tai Qing says: Heaven is something whose qi cannot yet be seen. Qian has Taichi (Supreme Ultimate) which is the Taishi (Grand Beginning). Taishi is the Grand Beginning. Taiyi is the beginning of qi. Taichu is when qi first becomes visible. Taishi is when form first becomes visible. Taisu is when substance first becomes visible. The beginning of form is the beginning of symptoms. The beginning of disease is the beginning of form. The Suwen says: From the Taiji (Supreme Ultimate), all was undifferentiated chaos. The Yijing says: Qian and Kun — the Yijing commentary says: The Supreme Ultimate gives birth to the Two Modes. It is said that from qi, form is complete, and from form, disease arises. From form life comes; from qi disease follows.

The undifferentiated merges and from the division of Qian and Kun arises the beginning. The Fang text says: Heaven's essence and earth's — the beginning. The child, in Qian (Heaven), when Heaven and Earth combine, Qian and Kun are listed together. From the Supreme Ultimate the Two are born.

The two essences — the beginning of the hun (ethereal soul) and the form — the spirit's beginning then transforms the ten thousand things.

The Beginning of Fetal Gestation
At the fifth month sinews form; at the sixth month bones form; at the third and seventh months the hun soul roams; at the fourth month movement is possible; the female [fetus] divides on the right into two essences.

At the eighth month the child's limbs separate; after the fourth [period] and nineteenth day, beginning from the fetus, after seven days the qi — and at nineteen days concern arises.

When yin and yang are fully established, the limbs separate at the fourth and nineteenth day. Beginning from the fetus, after seven days the qi — at nineteen the days of concern — when the month is full [birth occurs].

translation:
Therefore, when there are [numbers of days], those that have 230 or 280 days are upper-tier vessels. Those with 296 days are all superior vessels.

Heaven has the 23rd [cycle], with 238 days as the second hundred. Eighteen days, those with 294 or 296 days are all superior vessels.

When Heaven and Earth are not in accord, the fetus also cannot be formed. If the Earth likewise unites its virtue, then man must be born. This is the virtue of Heaven and Earth combining their qi.

On the Formation of the Four Great Elements

The Buddhist teaching says: The essence of earth, blood, fluids — all belong to the wind-harmony combining to form man. Sinews, bones, muscles, and flesh — all belong to the body's fire. The spirit-brightness then stirs. In the matter of chamber [relations], blood and fluid, borrowing the wind of essence — the four great elements combine, borrowing water and warmth, and life is produced through dryness.

Borrowing teeth and bones: the golden element, the great spirit — the water and wind grow abundant. Stirring essence, blood, and fluid — borrowing the wind — then cracking wind arises. The earth's abundance is as clouds and wind, the great qi of bones, like jade.

On the Waxing and Waning of Human Qi

At one year and ten years, the muscles and flesh begin to be firm. Blood and qi become settled, the flesh is even, and the pulse is full. Therefore one loves to walk and run. At forty years, the five viscera begin to settle. At thirty years, the six viscera flourish. At five and six years, the five viscera are established.

At ten years and fifteen years, the Yellow Emperor asked Qibo: "From the time a person is born, the true qi begins to flow, and the true qi resides below — therefore one loves to run. As one grows, the true qi begins to flow; when the true qi resides below, one loves to run."

translation:
Old Age and Childlessness

The viscera, bowels, and twelve channels: the liver energy peaks, then stabilizes; the knee's interstices begin to flourish and thrive, and the face and complexion bloom.

Therefore the qi begins to decline; the exterior and interior become thin; the white qi thins at the chest and diaphragm; the great surge calms to an even state.

The surface begins to suffer: the skin withers; decline begins at the surface and interior; the white qi thins at the chest.

The kidney qi causes the skin to become parched; decline begins; the surface suffers, the skin and flesh wither and decline.

The body's form gives rise to sourness; dwelling inwardly; within five years the pulse becomes vacuous and depleted.

Below, yin is deficient; phlegm and qi rise upward; the interior becomes replete and hollow; within nine years...

Then the sinews and bones begin to deteriorate; passing through six exhaustions and seven stages; as the body grows, the body declines; the yang vessels and heavenly dew dissipate; the upper five surfaces and the seven scorchings of the shoulders begin to whiten.

The time of decline: the bones begin to fall away; through six extremities and seven stages; in three intervals of seven days until the body becomes even; the pulse flows freely; the great seven: teeth grow, the pulse surges; monthly events begin.

When heaven no longer sustains the channels, the great thoroughfare vessel and the eight vessels decline; lesser yang qi and the heavenly dew are exhausted; the earthly way no longer flows; thus the form deteriorates and one can no longer bear children.

The sinews reach their fullness; essence and true qi are consolidated; the teeth fully emerge and grow to their utmost; at the four and eight count, the sinews, kidneys, and flanks surge with qi.

The viscera, bowels, and twelve channels begin to bloom at the surface; the face and complexion thrive.

Therefore qi begins to decline; the exterior and interior thin; the white qi thins at the chest; the great surge calms to evenness; the knee's interstices begin to flourish.

The skin withers; decline begins; the surface suffers and withers anew; decline resumes.

The kidney qi causes the skin to parch; the surface begins to suffer; the skin and flesh wither; decline begins.

The body's form gives rise to sourness; residing inwardly; within five years the pulse space becomes depleted. At one hundred years of age, all five viscera are exhausted, the spirit and qi have all departed, and only the bodily frame remains, until the end comes.

Not gaining years, gazing at forty, brightness at ten — the essence diminishes; at sixty-some years, half the years have passed.

text:
壽夭之異

肌內講壯五八腎氣盛，髮長齒更。六八陽氣衰竭於上，面焦髮鬢斑白。七八肝氣衰，筋不能動，天癸竭，精少，腎藏衰，形體皆極。八八則齒髮去。腎者主水，受五藏六府之精而藏之，故五藏盛乃能瀉。今五藏皆衰，筋骨解墮，天癸盡矣。故髮鬢白，身體重，行步不正，而無子耳。故五則藏齒髮盛，乃至能騰，跳者天癸，今主奚嗚

水鵠受精上藏五六府之形精，而斑藏白七，藏八肝氣隂齒社六八陽氣不能動，者天癸，今主

五白身體衰，動日作步不墮正，天而癸盡矣。故時聞而髮盡，故五則藏齒髮盛，乃至能騰，跳者天癸，今主

譬彼衰素，知時世以作勢法故異邪人陽將和失於之術，衔邪以數敖，飲伯食對以其妄夫鄉上古之居人皆百

其乃不知道時常務去作其愆逆精以乃散其盡不節，知持酒滿為常不醉時百

以御神務快以其心逆其元天以生其樂，務以弛精，無為為天地父命百父母半精，滿而不節，每天衰時

也以神務快地其務以弛散，無真節不故知半持百滿，常而不醉時百有人

命也。盛天者。父日人之元壽，天氣也各父有為天命，無存為故地半父百精，滿而不時衰，每天

之血盛，命者。盛義，天不同，故上人之元壽天氣，亦異有生之初，度氣，每天

天下之兩盛義者，當得故同，兩上中之壽，天亦能保異其偏盛者，當得中氣

天下折之雖壽，然受或氣風寒暑濕者之能感保外懼得飢飽下勞壽役不之然傷多
translation:
On the Differences Between Long and Short Life

At five times eight years (age 40), the kidney qi is abundant, the hair grows long and the teeth are renewed. At six times eight (age 48), the yang qi begins to decline from above, the face becomes sallow, and the hair at the temples turns white. At seven times eight (age 56), the liver qi declines, the sinews can no longer move freely, the heavenly essence (tiangui) is exhausted, semen diminishes, the kidney organ weakens, and the whole body reaches its limit. At eight times eight (age 64), the teeth and hair fall out. The kidneys govern water; they receive the essence of the five viscera and six bowels and store it, so only when the five viscera are flourishing can they discharge. Now that the five viscera have all declined, the sinews and bones are loose and weak, the heavenly essence is fully exhausted. Therefore the hair at the temples turns white, the body becomes heavy, the gait becomes unsteady, and one can no longer father children.

In antiquity, people who understood the Dao lived in accordance with yin and yang, harmonized with the arts of calculation and numerology, ate and drank in moderation, maintained regular habits in their daily life, did not exhaust themselves recklessly, and so were able to keep their bodies and spirits together, living out their natural years and passing away only after a hundred years.

People of today are not like this. They use wine as a beverage and treat reckless behavior as normal. In drunkenness they exhaust their essence; through dissipation they deplete their true vitality. They do not know how to hold to fullness, do not know how to govern their spirits, and are hasty in gratifying their hearts' desires. They go against the true joy of life, have no regular pattern in their activities, and so at half the proper age their vigor is already spent and they decline.

The heavenly lifespan allotted to each person at birth may differ — some receive more, some less, from the qi at the moment of birth. Those who receive a balanced and full endowment may attain the middle measure of long life. Those who receive an uneven endowment will attain less. Beyond this, exposure to wind, cold, heat, and dampness, as well as immoderate eating and drinking, overwork, and similar harms, will further shorten one's years.

text:
形氣定壽夭

于內草豈能一藥一盡乎扶票之生元氣也故上古聖年人

當也傳曰修身者化吉之者通仙醫明道而未當有已必須令人盡人事以副天天命也

則也以可以校得命而未必造化天能委之扶天命也

是以故醫者靈樞經曰形與氣相任則壽不相任則夭皮與肉果則壽血氣經則不

使者皮肉與經絡日形果則典形氣充形衰而充大則皮膚緩順也則形壽終天

克勝而形脈小小骨弱而者者勝夭吳氣衰形衰形氣充而大則充而克矣形無肌肉分不有顱分不起走形充形

而脈者骨小小則壽不者氣大吳形充而形氣充而大則大危肉充而形坚而有不分其不者追○霊形

者肉堅骨肉則脈勝夭則壽元°吳形矮充氣日其不人堅肯内而者

不壽性元脈肉膲縷緩而救°氣形充氣矮日而殺大人而其不分氣無肌肉分坚而有顱不者

亦急者多緩緩勝元大其人脈瘦日而殺大人氣囊充而殺氣性念念而脈

脹息數者亦急多天血内脈亦日緩大其抵人脈瘦日而殺大人囊矮充性念念而脈

神機易去多血神㯋日其抵人脈血脈念念而脈

掾神故多壽先也者論大江海之緩者則天地之呼吸晝夜難
translation:
On Determining Longevity and Short Life Through Form and Qi

Within the body, how could a single herb or single medicine be sufficient? To support and sustain life, one must nurture the primordial qi. Therefore, the sages of high antiquity lived long years.

It is said: one who cultivates the self transforms adversity into good fortune; one who penetrates this becomes like an immortal. The enlightened physician understands this way, and though one cannot guarantee it, one must always instruct people to exhaust all human effort, in order to assist Heaven's mandate.

Therefore, the physician's role: the Lingshu Jing states that when form and qi are proportionate to each other, one lives long; when they are not proportionate, one dies early. When skin and flesh are firm, one lives long; when the blood and vessels are diminished, one dies early.

When skin, flesh, and channels are proportionate — when form is substantial — then form and qi are full together, and when form declines while qi remains full, the skin and flesh become loose, and form will end at its heaven-allotted time.

When the vessels overcome the bones, and the bones are small and the pulse is weak, qi declines — form declines — when form and qi are full and large, there is danger. When the flesh is full and form is firm, portions are unequal...

When bones and flesh are firm, the pulse overcomes — longevity. When form is short and qi is sparse, the person is thin and wasting away...

When one is restless and the breathing is rapid, when the spirit mechanism is easily lost, blood and spirit are depleted by day — this is a sign of shortened life.

When the spirit mechanism governs the great rivers and seas of the body, their ebb and flow, then Heaven and Earth's rhythm of inhalation and exhalation, day and night, flows without difficulty.

text:
人身猶一國

分則一百位抱计子宫室日也一四人之身别一國郊境家骨腹之

也满也神夫猶君也其民也臣也其氣猶民所以臣安也其國猶民惜也其他氣知治骨節之也

只故二天升地二降而已人之無窮吸畫夜一萬三千五百亦不

以全其身散則是國以至滅起死之後患者病不可難生

身能治百失則國民所删消安也其國猶民惜也其他氣知治而所

以以全而疾亡全其身能治百失則國民所删消以至滅起死之後患者病不可難生

百根養之而疾易而疾不以共無散事而易濁人故能拔逆之以所大治徒後患者病不可難生保人社難

明謀慮出萬肺腎者相傳之官正之官決斷出焉肝者將軍之官謀慮出焉心一臣官神疏

者之官専樂出焉膵出萬者中傳之官受官盛五味出焉腸者物大出焉化焉水

道禹臂尊官传出万膀胱者州都之官津液藏焉氣化則能出矣
translation:
The Human Body Is Like a State

The body has a hundred positions, each like a subsidiary of the central court. Just as a state has a ruler, ministers, and people, the body has its organs arranged in a similar hierarchy. The ruler corresponds to the heart; the ministers to the various organs; the people to the qi that flows through the body. When these are in harmony, the state is at peace; when disordered, the state falls into ruin. The qi of the people is like the vitality of the nation — when it is cherished and preserved, the nation endures; when it is neglected, decline follows.

Heaven and Earth rise and fall; a person's breath cycles through day and night, thirty thousand five hundred times — or thereabouts — without cease.

When the body is whole and unified, it can govern the hundred ailments; when it is scattered and fragmented, it is like a state collapsing from within — the dead cannot be revived, and illnesses become incurable, as disasters arise one after another. Only by preserving the person and nurturing the community can hardship be averted.

Clarity of counsel and deliberation belong to the lungs and kidneys, which are the organs of transmission and regulation. Decisions and judgments originate from them. The liver is the organ of the general — strategy and planning are its domain. The heart oversees the spirit and channels its workings.

The spleen governs the flavors of the five tastes. The intestines govern the transformation and passage of matter, and the bladder is the organ of the provincial capital, storing fluids; when the qi transforms properly, it is able to discharge them.

text:
丹田有三

丹田人之神府也天地之丹田上下丹田心為精宮府中也丹田藏絲之宮中也丹田

養則仙經曰腦下三府為天下海者上丹田下丹田心藏絲精宮府中丹田也

則十二生則壽使天下闢者塞其而不大道形乃大戒傷之以此

失九比十三宮者不得以相失也故主明則下安以

氣鑄而成開精生於神精故形統神形已身之中若以精氣神而為主生就陰陽真篇

治腎形統神精生於精故一身之中以秀氣神而為主生無過於陰篇

為治神精形統三首物形一身真氣已交而邪神康主節乎其神中統之心無生之氣道統煉

也為腎精形統神首物形一身真氣已交而邪神康主節乎其神中統之心無生之氣道統煉

背有三關

仙經曰背後有三關曰尾閭後關曰夾脊中關曰玉枕上關皆精氣升降往來之道路也若得其樞篇之機無運則上下金鼎煉道白朮片循環如一脈朝漿泥

天來河之道轉路也若得翕升之柄篇之機無運則上下金鼎煉道白朮片循環如一脈朝漿泥

九泥之通上紫金三鼎來柄篇之機無運則上下
translation:
The Three Cinnabar Fields (Dantian)

The cinnabar field (dantian) is the spirit palace of a person. Heaven and earth have their dantian; the upper and lower dantian, with the heart serving as the palace of essence and spirit at the center, and the dantian storing the palace of refined essence within.

If one nourishes them, the immortal classics say: below the brain are three palaces that serve as the sea of heaven below. The upper dantian, lower dantian, and the heart are the palace storing refined essence; the middle dantian as well.

When the twelve are cultivated, one attains longevity. If one unblocks the heavenly passages and clears obstructions, and does not obstruct them, then the great Way takes form, and one observes great precautions against injury.

Failing these, one loses the nine, and compared to the thirteen palaces, one cannot obtain what is needed, and loses relatedness. Therefore, when the master is clear and bright, those below are at peace.

Essence is cast and formed; spirit-essence is born through the refined spirit, and thus spirit unifies form. When essence, vital breath, and spirit already communicate within the body, and with these as the master of life — arising from yin and yang — as the true compendium states.

The Three Passes of the Back

The immortal classics say: along the back there are three passes. The first is called the Caudal Pass (weilü), the posterior pass. The second is called the Spinal Pass (jiaji), the middle pass. The third is called the Jade Pillow Pass (yuzhen), the upper pass. All are pathways along which essence and vital breath ascend and descend, coming and going. If one obtains the pivot and mechanism, and the movement flows without obstruction, then above and below, the golden cauldron refines the Way, circulating continuously like one pulse flowing up to the mud-pill palace (niwan) at the crown.

text:
保養精氣神

流入口香甜清泰下遍古端不○同契註曰人身氣水至于地膽中而行不蓋蟾蜍珠下畫夜端不停鶴江穴之日水流通東

血循環仙也曰精神者身之本氣者神之用形者氣之宅無義太神而氣太神則形調氣者主形亦相知往名也大神之行者氣之調形者神則主之神因也無而義太神

勢則衰形絕以人長生者太身用之也閑也氣者用之調之形者神則主也神因也無而義太神也大川月乃神之行也亦然通

衰則形絕以人長生立生生者太身用之也閑也歌者用之調形者神則主之因也無而義太神者也

努則以形乃是而以人長長者者太也閑也者用調形神則主之神因也無而義太神也

生偏馬者不全宅鎮以神安而有修養也無神之不形館者不免者嚮於神之能加散於宅

堤境遊游覽者城水不形觀魂安夫之所者養也也者形火不不陰居也嚮神之氣能加散宅

服百氣形不能死食卵味飛氣於清天則食神嗽夷者形陽千勠碉者不不居也嚮神之氣能加散宅

歸本地人生之同死魂飛天則神嗽夷千勠碉者則者不居也嚮神之氣能加散宅

蘇如一銀之太本以同體魂飛天食神嗽形陽千勠碉者不不居也嚮於神之氣能加散宅

體全然之理地生之死同體魂飛天食神嗽形陽千百碉者不免者嚮於神之氣能加散宅

精氣則性命長存養其者生之烟則本精氣反則萬物沈亦熹熹

36
translation:
Preserving and Nourishing the Essence, Vital Breath, and Spirit

The text begins with a commentary stating: The human body's vital breath circulates like water reaching the earth's interior, moving without ceasing, like the toad and pearl [reflected in water], day and night without pause — this is what the "Crane River Inscription" refers to when it speaks of the body's circulation reaching through every passage.

The spirit and essence are the root of the body; vital breath (qi) is the function of the spirit; and form (the physical body) is the dwelling of qi. Without the spirit, the great spirit cannot exist; without the great spirit, the form cannot be regulated. Qi is what governs the form; the spirit presides over qi. Because of the spirit, there is no lack — the great spirit and its meaning, the spirit's movement, regulates form as well.

The decline of vitality causes the form to wither and life to be cut short. Those who attain long life do so because they preserve the great spirit within the body; they guard and regulate qi; they keep the spirit as master of the form; and because of the spirit, nothing is lacking.

One who exerts great effort brings decline to the form, cutting off life. Those who achieve longevity and sustained life do so by preserving the great spirit in the body, keeping the functions of breath regulated and form under the spirit's governance.

The physical dwelling must be kept as the home of the spirit in peace and rest. To cultivate and nourish is to keep the spirit within — if the spirit departs from its dwelling, it disperses.

Qi that is piled high at the banks and in the still waters: if the form loses its spirit, the hun-soul flies away; without the spirit, the form becomes an empty house; the spirit's breath scatters from its dwelling.

One who takes in the hundred breaths and cultivates the form must not let the spiritual breath fly off into the sky; then the spirit will remain and nourish the form — otherwise it disperses from its dwelling.

Returning to the original ground, the life of a person — living and dying — the hun-soul flies to heaven; if the spirit remains, it continues to nourish the form.

Like silver and its source, with the body as one — life and death, the hun-soul's flight — if the spirit is preserved, it nourishes form through the breath.

The whole body in its natural principle: life and death, the hun-soul, spirit nourishing form — all through the breath.

When essence and qi are complete, one's nature and life endure long. Those who cultivate and nourish themselves keep their life-force rising; when essence and qi return and are complete, the ten thousand things settle and are at rest.

text:
古有真人至人聖人賢人

氣獨立守神肌肉若一故能壽敝天地無有終時此其道生。

此聽道於八遠四時去之世時有一至故人壽逝全神惠天地無有咢時。

觀視陽於其八以世有之聖益天地積壽精全神惠天地和有然時。

真欲於以於世間之者盡天地壽命和從行地理於間處時。

普欲姿務觀以於為無事內心不從入風之地亦世舉道於。

愉不數從其次以自谷外為勞形形體皆真天不勢內心精神亦思散亦可以格。

百益從此時陰有别分别者四時法则天不勢上地象似日月亦列星。

展時壽遊大往而上有古聖人之教下也謂之精虛都眼內守。

有使益之上於古時格無真氣皆從之精虛都眼內守。

論上古天真

癡倦安氣從赤是順以各志從其而皆愁都悲面而故差其形勞任而風。

其服樂氣從以是順以各志從閒而少皆慮悲心安顔而故差養形勞任而。

不能勞務其目滿那下不相慕其心愿智賢不肖不懼於物。

其不能感其民故曰朴是以嗜慾不能勞其目淫邪不能惑其心愿智賢不肖不懼於物。
translation:
In ancient times there were True People, Perfected People, Sages, and Worthy People.

Some stood alone, preserving their spirit, their flesh and muscles as one, and thus were able to live out their years alongside Heaven and Earth, with no end to their time — this was their Way of life.

Others heard the Way at a great distance, in the four seasons, departing from the mundane world; in their time there were those who reached full longevity, keeping their spirit whole and their virtue in accord with Heaven and Earth, without any diminishment of their time.

Others observed the yang forces, aligned with the world's sages, accumulated merit with Heaven and Earth, preserved their essence fully, kept their spirit whole, and remained in harmony with Heaven and Earth through the natural seasons.

The truly desirous aligned themselves with the world, among its people, exhausting the measure of Heaven and Earth, their lives and fates in accord, following the patterns of the earth and the order between things.

Harmonizing desires through virtuous conduct, observing and practicing, not straining through affairs, keeping the heart untroubled, not following the winds of the world — likewise understanding the world's principles and the Way.

Pleasantly, without excess, following in turn, being content within, not laboring the form fruitlessly — the body whole, the essence and spirit likewise undispersed, thoughts not scattered, all may reach the standard.

The hundred benefits follow; through the seasons, the yin and yang are distinguished separately; the four seasons follow the rules of Heaven and Earth — like the sun, moon, and arrayed stars.

Advancing through the years of long life, moving through the vastness — above there were the ancient sages whose teachings came down: this is called preserving the essential vacancy, guarding within.

Having received the benefits above: in ancient times, the sage's standard, the true qi all follows; preserving the essential vacancy, guarding within.

Discussion on the True Essence of High Antiquity

Foolish fatigue and unsettled qi follow; thus, going along with the will in each matter, with little worry or sorrow, the face composed, correcting the form, the labor assigned accordingly — with the wind.

Those who serve and take pleasure follow likewise; going along with the will in each matter, with little worry or sorrow, the heart at peace, the face composed, correcting and nourishing the form, the labor assigned accordingly.

Unable to toil and weary the eyes, not drawn into evil below, not envying one another — the heart wishes that the wise and the unwise alike do not fear external things.

Because the people are thus, they are called simple. Therefore, desires cannot fatigue their eyes, lewd and deviant things cannot confuse their hearts; whether wise or unworthy, they do not fear external things.

translation:
The Four Seasons and Regulating the Spirit

When one acts against the movements of nature and does not accord with the Way, one loses the ability to preserve one's full span of years; all such people court peril and danger, and cannot reach a hundred years of age. The flourishing of living things requires that one not act contrary to the night's rhythm.

To defy the teachings of Heaven and Earth will injure the liver. In summer one should abide by the heat, but if one allows cold to enter, this causes the body's warming energies to scatter and be lost — the form becomes as if weakened, and the will and vitality of living things are dispersed.

To go against the season in which things flower and grow — acting as if it were summer when things are in bloom, or cold when one should be warm — causes one to lose the vitality of spring and age prematurely, which is called "growing old before one's time."

In the three months of a season, the heart should be kept calm and at peace; this is what is called nurturing the qi of autumn. If the mind is tranquil and the spirit settled, the heavenly qi is peaceful.

The spirit and the luminous qi should be harmonized; if one fails to do so, the lung is injured by the autumn harvest energies. One who stores energy in spring cultivates the yang in summer; in autumn one gathers in, in winter one stores away — this is the root of yin and yang.

In the second and third months, one should not expose oneself to harsh conditions; the will should not be burdened. If the skin and flesh are afflicted, one must retire early in autumn, gathering and storing inward.

When the sage follows the cycle of the four seasons — growing in spring, nurturing in summer, harvesting in autumn, storing in winter — he honors the root of living things. Therefore the sage nurtures life in spring, fosters growth in summer, gathers in autumn, and stores in winter. Spring is birth, summer is growth, autumn is harvest, winter is storage: this is the Way of the ten thousand things, the cycle of beginning and end.

text:
以道療病

之死則生奇之本也起是之謂災害生從
則生之神得道仙之有古今之聖醫者醫能療人之疾而不使知不
療疾人愈之心不是循本也一逮時未不窮其源而攻其世俗欲
求療疾人必庸醫切其心忘亦乃取貧也於太白一使真病人者盡欲洽心其疾應治其此則世源不
心必正其心忘下一切不於道白一使真病人者盡欲洽心中疾疑治其此則世俗欲
之過想惡一便切妄念心一平我切合悟所患之生天野為久思其
萬之事遂皆是於神則自終日自然心為君泰寧而我地和平世間久為
然虛解幽福皆空虛則自無有日然心為君泰寧而我知和我平身世世間是
則法藥未到又曰病地是自無有日然清淨死為管是安性然我領世地是問
大則後後至於人忘矣此病人以先道治症能如怎
法後治於飢病之先治家治療然安
源病之一未者曰治心以先醫家治療於已
由則病之後日日修療者雖治之法有二養而治病之已
因心而末生也不
translation:
Treating Illness Through the Way (Dao)

Between death and life lies something wondrous; this is the true foundation. To rise above this is what is meant by calamity and harm — life follows from this.

The spirit of life attains the Way. The immortals of old and the sages and physicians of today — those physicians who can treat people's illnesses and yet not let them know — do not merely address the surface symptoms while ignoring the source, attacking the illness while the people of the world merely desire a cure.

When seeking to heal illness, if the physician is ordinary, he cuts off his mind's wandering thoughts; he must also draw on the teaching of Tao — letting the true patient exhaust their desire to harmonize the heart, and the illness, being contemplated, will be resolved. The foundation must be restored.

The heart must be upright; all wandering thoughts must be set aside — cut off all below, do not dwell on the Tao. Let the true patient exhaust their desire to harmonize the heart — the illness in the mind, when reflected upon and treated, will dissolve the worldly desires.

Passing thoughts, evil notions — once cut off, let the heart wander no more; in one moment of peace, I cut through, merge with, and awaken to all afflictions. Life in the world between heaven and earth — one long contemplation.

The ten-thousand affairs all proceed emptily; the spirit becomes settled, naturally the heart becomes the ruler, peaceful and still, knowing harmony, and the body and world become one.

The Dharma and medicine have not yet arrived, but the mind-ground is naturally free, pure, and clear; death becomes manageable; the ruler is peaceful and still.

The great method: after illness, after recovery, one arrives — the person forgets; through this method, one treats the mind first, then the physician and household treatment follows.

The source of illness: first treat the household, then the treatment follows of itself.

From the root, illness arises from the heart — life itself is not separate from this.

text:
虛心合道

白王蟾曰一人無心則有道而無合有心則與道不遠

役竭有天地惟此無能大役能無役而至能無形有識精役無形能役有陽數萬物妙不能役無形能役形有阻難能役形陽萬物妙能役形不難

理無者數有百念若紀起鍊役形有識妙不能役神今疑夫修此

忘之立聚氣則丹成氣以形固妙有神忘固神則疑神識全神今故只實此齊此

聚物之何一忘曰虛字一升則養成氣丹後成形有形以養神形之謂來手無調本元四萬三千

百書盧是其物也之本斗之墻也壽本元四陽萬真三氣

學道無早晚

本草重三百人八百夜欲十動作四苑鍊也也又易失內應乎不乾純至六之

極陽求倶少畫百百餘日日喫一者物二之斗

再接方始一陰六得十二四人十歲歲用老老真怕怕死沒補即汝返道遇劉海

馬自然到

復則不雖遠一陰百不極則十年老老猶不可生還遇乾明如師指老運用樹訣用心苦

四人陽倶不死亦晚年乎到八刲不卦壽數則已
translation:
Emptying the Heart and Uniting with the Dao

Master Bai Yuchan said: A person who has no [self-centered] heart/mind then has the Dao, yet may not be united with it. A person who has a [self-centered] heart/mind is not far from the Dao either.

[On the role of spirit and form:] Only Heaven and Earth are without limit in their capacity to act. The Dao can act without acting, can be without form yet possess awareness, can direct the refined spirit, can be formless yet direct form, can direct the Yang and the myriad things — wondrous and without obstacle. It is difficult to direct form; one must direct the spirit. If the spirit is whole, doubt dissolves; if the spirit is nourished, the divine awareness is complete.

[On gathering qi and forming the elixir:] Forget outward things; establish gathering of qi; then the elixir is formed. Qi nourishes form; form nourishes the spirit. This is what is called returning to the origin — the primordial Four and the myriad three-thousand [subtle breaths].

Learning the Dao Is Never Too Early or Too Late

The Bencao [classic] says: One who practices three hundred days and eight hundred nights of inner cultivation, moving and working [in accordance with the method], refining through the cycle, will naturally achieve it. Each day consuming only a little, one hundred and some days, eating and drinking moderately — this is the measure.

[On the cycle of yin and yang in cultivation:] Beginning with one yin, through six [cycles], reaching ten, then twenty, four people, ten years — old and aging, yet fearing death no longer. Returning along the path, one encounters [the immortals] Liu and Hai.

[On the stages:] One yin, one hundred [days], reaching the extreme, then ten years — though old, one can still return. Meeting [a teacher] clear as a mirror, like a master pointing the way — the old find use in returning, using the mind with diligence.

Four people [who cultivate] yang together do not die; even in late years, one reaches the point of no aging. The eight trigrams and the count of one's lifespan — this is already accomplished.

text:
人心合天機

端傳以長生之頁訣逐得悟真於無窮矣何人乃陽武六騎十之

則是特正陽真人遇菊海翁太十四歲金丹之道賴真人成威馬

自四燕歲大十四歲方十四歲像金丹而真道人成威

積仙符至仙至十六皆精方年得修道劉海仙翁太方十四歲金丹真道而人成威

世大人道嗜於慈衰十於精思得道金而真成壯道年之賴真人而人成

閒早得年求下道速十修四成之前神亦疲難勢傳仙精成功氣偽真陽之氣絕能絕慾失若持大戒難

師選心論即日道庵及絕色身末亦難勢傳仙精成功氣偽真陽之氣絕能絕慾失若持大戒難放難

造也非人靜機之心此乃天也以心運之天道知即道得未能遇以心道

五日行化順惱心論即日道度以以心為萬貫用天道知即道得未能遇以心道

上頤下轉署海中戊度陰陽故天得宜飛乾○運之天圍四於時此也者是以為心道

運片時因地下轉署海中此天也心以心貫用天道知即道得未能遇以心道

心為機只謂半衣于陽初動之時也天機將至人能勤吾天以陽除不天御為心道

機心謂半衣于陽初動於身中日稿人機心若天天心合為顛月歲本日不天御為
translation:
The Human Heart Merges with the Mechanism of Heaven

It is transmitted that through the formulas for long life, one can gradually attain enlightenment about the true nature of the infinite. What person then is the Yang Warrior of the Six Riders and Ten?

This is specifically the True Person of Correct Yang, who encountered the Chrysanthemum Sea Elder when he was fourteen years old, and through the Way of the Golden Elixir, relying on the True Person, he matured and achieved completion.

From youth, at the age of fourteen, following the method of the fourteen years, modeling the Golden Elixir, and through the true Way, one achieves full strength and maturity.

Accumulating immortal talismans, reaching the sixteenth year, all refined, through the method of the year, obtaining the cultivation of the Way — Liu Hai the Immortal Elder — through the great method of fourteen years, the true Way of the Golden Elixir, one matures as a person.

Among the great men of the world, those devoted to the Way, though in decline and in their weariness at the tenth year of refinement, through focused thought they obtain the Way of Gold, and through true achievement they become robust — through the years, relying on the True Person, the person achieves completion.

In the early years of seeking, descending the Way quickly through ten cultivations, four completions, before the spirit, even though exhausted and hard-pressed, transmitting the essence of the immortals, perfecting merit and energy — but the false True Yang energy, once cut off, can completely sever desire; yet if one loses it, if one holds to the great precepts with difficulty, it is hard to release.

The master selects the mind's discourse, immediately the daily Way of the hermitage, and utterly cuts off form and body — though it remains difficult to transmit, the essence of the immortals, perfecting merit and energy — but false True Yang energy, once cut off, can sever desire completely, yet holding to the great precepts remains difficult.

Creation is not a human stillness — the mechanism of the mind: this is none other than Heaven itself. Using the mind to move it, the Heavenly Way knows; immediately the Way obtains what it could not yet encounter — using the mind as the Way.

Five days of practicing transformation, following order with a troubled mind — the daily discourse of the Way's degree — with the mind one penetrates and uses the Heavenly Way; immediately the Way knows what it could not yet encounter.

Above the chin, turning downward through the heat of the sea within — the degree of the hidden yin and yang — thus Heaven obtains what is proper to fly and rise. The movement of Heaven surrounds the four, and at that time — this is it — using the mind as the Way.

Moving in fragments of time, following the ground downward through the heat of the sea within: this is Heaven itself. The mind penetrates and uses the Heavenly Way; immediately the Way knows what it could not yet encounter.

The heart is the mechanism. Only calling it "half-clothed in yang" — at the first moment of movement, the Heavenly Mechanism is about to arrive. A person who can diligently practice will, through yang, eliminate what is not Heaven's, and govern through the mind as the Way.

The mechanism of the mind — calling it "half-clothed in yang" — at the first stirring within the body, in the daily manuscript: a person's mechanism of mind, if Heaven and the mind unite as one, turns the moon year by year, rooted in the daily, not heaven-governed, steered through the mind as the Way.

text:
搬運

之又候復上機以于之則天人合一發氣內外相符結而為一陽矣

又之候當夫應之人欲日為人之信也迴之初養神樞此生之道各家有其法調之全大

服食聚養全商氣聚全神和是便血脈暢也每神氣疾定鳴時三之道各搬運補華數全之法

精息便叫神覺身滿各便當大脈自然下流通當此之丹以補轉華元也以調十

水遍生如滿乃行運氣神覺身滿各便當大脈自然下流通當此之丹田以補搬運華元也

令熱乃行通引起一道法平行首單補養熟然納入丹此之搬運補華元也以轉調

陽訓不可食章一遵了行之妙當行首大補養熟然納入丹田之搬運補華元也乃手以揉香擦

大略不可坐不可食過一道以通道法步行單補養藥納入丹此之搬運補華元也乃手以揉香擦

然訓調不可坐面不東知出腹以手步行單補約方可的顏臉兩丹乃手以揉香擦

用便杖鼻上內微納之呼吟。單出腹內舊幾三服兩食三步日百待然后此高三養五

燕不下自舌上內微存清氣呼吟。此出腹內舊幾三服兩食三步日百待然後後腎停后養生

前不及亦實前為之亦可此時數為津液歸為丹亦田可又卧中氣咳向歸亦田可又曰後人丑
translation:
On the Method of Conducting and Circulating Qi (Bànyùn)

Again, at this moment, when one returns to the fundamental mechanism, one applies it to the principle of Heaven and Man uniting as one — the qi arises, inner and outer correspond, and they consolidate into a single Yang.

Again, at this time one must apply it: a person who wishes to cultivate must daily act as a person of trust and faith. One returns to the initial stage of nourishing the spirit. This pivot is the way of life; each family has its own methods. In general, the whole is great.

For the intake of food and nourishment: accumulate nourishment and fully gather the qi, gather the spirit fully — then the blood and pulse flow freely. Each time the spirit and qi are stabilized, at the right time, by means of this path, through the practice of conducting and transporting, one replenishes the essence at the elixir field.

The breath should be made fine; the spirit awakens; the whole body fills; all becomes easy; the great pulse flows naturally downward; when it passes through this, the elixir field is replenished and the transporting of vital essence is regulated.

Warm the qi and let it circulate; guide and raise it along one channel; walk in the method of moving the head; singly supplement and nourish; let it naturally be received into the elixir field — this is the method of conducting and replenishing the vital essence at the origin.

One must guide and regulate; one must not sit still; one must not eat excessively along the single channel; use the method of steps to guide; singly supplement the medicinal herbs received into the elixir field — this is the transporting method; then use the hands to rub and massage.

Use the staff; the nose, above the interior; store the fine breath; call and sigh. Single: push out the abdomen, the old interior; three doses, two meals, three steps, one hundred days, then wait; afterward nourish the kidneys, stop, then nurture life.

Before, not reaching, thus truly before, being such, one can — at this time the fluids return to the elixir field; one can also lie down; the qi coughing returns to the elixir field; again one can — afterward, at the Ox hour (1–3 AM), the person rises.

text:
按摩導引

能常食玉泉令人長年面有光色。玉泉者口中津液也。朝旦未起早漱津令滿口乃吞之。琢齒二七遍。如此者乃名練精。

仙泉。旦時漱津。常以舌柱上齶。使水滿口乃吞之。

卅玉泉。手按鼻左右。上下以引鼻中鼻涕出盡。乃引咽嚥之。七遍從早朝以

又日。九遍。每朝以二手從耳。朝服之膳。

通。又嚥唾。每遇九七。從

又日。叩齒九遍。上下常數十。通過九遍。

又。旦興。以手按目四眥。令人目明。去風。頭眼頻熱。試眼有二七謂之遍。

令耳聰。目去年然。無又停日。復熱摩明。手去心。頭上開。引氣以頭鼻嚥之。

使人耳聰。目延自年然。無停。警熱摩明。面表上然供。風熱澤。頻眼每上二七謂之遍。

令庭梨連。鼻變。耳輪上不遍面。表上然供熱澤。頻試頭。

於天補潤潤。以手防摩職耳輪。上不遍面。表然供熱澤。

苦岳鄰氣以補潤。防摩職耳。有遍數。所謂閉目後其謂括。

城中以礎擾聲。兩固神哩職。繾繿繿繿。令韓閉叩頂鳴。鳴鼓鼓。

心三坐。十礎。以礎擾聲響。兩固神哩。繾繿欲令韓閉叩頂鳴鼓。

左右。織天天柱。齘二十。四度。抱覺。鳴銕鈷。膺一兩。斛杓泌龍心。攬橺橺。水潭酏斛觥觗嫳叙。

微擺天天柱齘二十。四拊覺。鳴銕鈷。膺一兩斛。赤龍攬橺橺。水潭酏斛觗嫳。

十五

四三
translation:
Massage and Breathing Exercises (Anma Doin)

Regularly drinking the Jade Spring enables a person to live long and have a radiant complexion. The Jade Spring refers to the saliva in the mouth. Each morning before rising, rinse the saliva until the mouth is full, then swallow it. Tap the teeth twenty-seven times. Doing this is called "refining the essence."

Immortal Spring: At dawn, rinse the saliva. Habitually press the tongue against the upper palate until the mouth fills with fluid, then swallow it.

Jade Spring method: Press the sides of the nose left and right, moving up and down, to draw out all nasal discharge. Then swallow it down. Seven repetitions, beginning each morning.

Also: Nine times daily. Each morning use both hands from the ears. Take it as a morning supplement.

Also: Swallow saliva. Each time, nine times seven repetitions.

Also: Tap the teeth nine times. Upper and lower together, repeatedly up to ninety passes.

Also: Upon rising, press the corners of all four eye sockets with the hands. This brightens the eyes, dispels wind, and relieves heat in the head and eyes. The method is done twenty-seven times; this is called one round.

For sharp hearing: Let the ears be clear. Remove yearly accumulation. Without stopping. Rub with warm hands over the face, bring in qi through the nose and swallow it.

Make the ears acute and the eyes clear: Do this every year without stopping. Rub warming hands over the face, supply warmth and moisture. Rub the eyes twenty-seven times, called one round.

Rub the nose bridge and ears: Rotate over the ear lobes, not stopping until the face surface becomes naturally warm and moist.

With hands supplement and moisten: Use the hands to rub the ear lobes repeatedly. Close the eyes afterward; this is what is called the bracket method.

City center drumming: Fix both hands firmly, silently close and tap the crown, making the sound of a drum.

Sit with three mind centers: Firmly fix both hands, rub and produce resonance, close and tap the crown, making the drum sound.

Left and right: Shake the heavenly pillar vertebrae twenty times. Four repetitions. Feel the ringing sensation. The Red Dragon (tongue) stirs the saliva. Rinse and swallow.

Gently shake the heavenly pillar vertebrae twenty times. Four repetitions. The Red Dragon stirs and gathers saliva. Rinse and swallow.

translation:
Key Teachings on Cultivating Health and Nourishment

[The text presents a series of instructions on the art of preserving health, organized into numbered categories:]

One overall principle: Close the mouth, regulate the breath, harmonize the body's energies with the teacher's guidance; nourish the vital fluid; the thirty-six divine waters flow through the channels.

[On expelling evil influences:] Drive out deviant forces; after swallowing repeatedly, follow the sequence step by step, going through the eight trigrams before and after, transforming through the process of Creation and the forces of Heaven and Earth (qian and kun).

[On cultivating vitality:] Purify the fire within; regulate and adjust the hundred pathways; through the three primary energies, keep the pulse steady; bow the head low, extend the right and left legs and feet, relax and open the mouth; regulate and cut off the breath; perform the needle-like and massaging movements.

[On nourishing the four essentials:]
First — nourish essence (jing) and fluids; keep the complexion true and genuine.
Second — nourish the five organs' vital energies.
Third — nourish the refined spirit (qi-wen) for three days.
Fourth — nourish with sparse words and frugal speech; nourish internally.

The vital primordial energy (yuan qi) is complete; the spirit (shen) should be kept tranquil, with few desires. The five senses should be used sparingly; cultivate the spirit's vitality through food and drink.

The yellow [elixir] can be obtained; one who follows the True Way through nine cycles of practice will not die. Those who cultivate the middle [center of the body], who taste and guard it, must above all not overdo it.

Vital energy sustains the ten thousand forms of life; the breath arises from the spirit's flourishing; eating and drinking sustain this.

[Seasonal and practical notes on summer heat, water intake, entering the energy gates, illness management, and sequential movement exercises for the head, neck, legs, and feet, with breath control and self-massage techniques, follow in abbreviated form.]

translation:
The text is from the Dongui Bogam on the cultivation of one's nature and health preservation. It discusses the following themes:

The pivot (pivotal teaching): One should regularly practice: clacking the teeth, regulating the breath in the head, cultivating stillness of essence and spirit. These are the five or six daily practices of the immortal sages.

A person can sustain life by eliminating three poisons — thereby preserving life, prolonging longevity, and allowing the spirit to become naturally clear and still, and of itself serene.

On desires and harm: If one does not listen to extremes, there will be no deception; if one is greedy and labors excessively, the emotions multiply; excessive desire damages the essence; anger harms the spirit. One should aim to reduce desires, reduce labor, and allow the emotions to settle into stillness and tranquility.

On the nine prohibitions for the sick: Those who are ill should not listen to sounds to the extreme, nor look with their eyes to the extreme. The way of nurturing one's nature is difficult — one should not eat to satiety; one should not overindulge in food and drink.

On the five difficulties: Fame and profit are hard to abandon; joy and anger are hard to eliminate; sound and beauty are hard to discard; flavors and richness are hard to moderate; the spirit scattering due to overabundance is hard to steady. These are called the five difficulties. Without these five difficulties, one may achieve longevity.

On Sun Simiao's teachings on cultivating one's nature: The way of nourishing one's nature is difficult. Even those who know the techniques of nourishing the body and practice them still find it difficult to achieve long life. The key principle: one should always desire to do a little — not to the point of exhaustion. Do not strain the eyes, do not overexert through movement. Prolonged extremes of any kind damage longevity. As the Dongshen Zhenjing (Scripture of the Cavern Spirit) says: prolonged extremes in anything diminish one's lifespan.

translation:
The Method of Internal Cultivation of the Returned Elixir (Huandan Neilian Fa)

The meaning of cultivating life lies not in damaging the body — this is the foundation for nearing old age. The art of longevity in young years relies on supplementing what is lacking; for advancing in years, it relies on nourishing the vital breath (qi); to guard life against weakness, one must reach toward these principles.

By managing the scenery of the meridians, dwelling in a state of spiritual tranquility, responding to danger, guarding against it, welcoming the budding of [vital force] — this is the art of separating from [ordinary] life. In youth, avoid losses; use supplementation to advance in years; use the cultivation of qi to overcome weakness, and so guard life.

The surplus [of essence] — guard it yourself, supplement it yourself, and benefit from it. Thus one achieves longevity of qi and blood. This is called Golden Water.

The Cinnabar Field (dantian) — because of the scroll it is said: thereby the Returned Elixir accumulates its fluid. This is called Golden Water.

The Returned Elixir and the Cinnabar Field — nightly [the essence] is a gift. It is said that the one who [cultivates] the lung and the embryo — because of the scroll there is the saying: the Returned Elixir and its fluid. This is called Golden Water.

Enter the wondrous formula: nightly, the dragon rises deep; the lung and embryo [are nourished]; through the scrolls it is recorded — the Returned Elixir and its fluid, this is called Golden Water.

Pour it into the mud-pill [palace at the crown]; at the time of the fire blazing in the furnace, urgently listen: the Returned Elixir — test the Cinnabar Field. Know that the Golden Fluid is the mother, the elixir fluid is the mother.

Halt at the Yellow Gate, guard the small [aperture]; by the method of nodal intervals, through a thousand refinements, the Tiger and Earth [elements] — this too returns to the Golden Fluid, which is truly the mother of the elixir liquid.

Day by day, circulate; through great fire, at the critical juncture, one attains it by pushing and guiding — the Capital [of the body]. At times of stillness, test the Cinnabar Field; the Worthy Gold is the mother of water, the mother of the elixir liquid.

Like moving through wine, rising upward, the sensation reaches the coccyx (weilü) — like a knife. From this [nourishment] flows through pathways, resembling snow-white egrets crossing a river. Listen — the Returned Elixir; the Cinnabar Field — know that the Golden Fluid is the mother.

Observe the stored [essence in the] organs; through the elixir's cycles, it softens the body, and one feels as if fed, as though the nine apertures and the center of the mouth are nourished — the body like a vessel of water, rising and bubbling, the song says: more and more Golden Fluid.

Also, the image of water — within this, at the mouth [of the cavity], it is called Hua Di (Flower Ground). From the Rushui point, the next [stage] follows without cessation; there is the Golden Spirit and Jade Flower — this opens the eyes inward to the water landscape.

The Returned Elixir — its surging, unceasing, then there is the Golden Spirit, the Jade Flower of the body — this opens inwardly to the water landscape within.

Like a candle, like constancy, like granules — Golden granules descend, returning. The mouth center is fumigated and nourished; it is easy to nourish the true countenance, filtering and cleansing, washing [the body].

translation:
Prohibitions and Cautions for Cultivating One's Nature

The method: spirit issues forth through the eyes — this is called the eyes being the windows of the mind. The nose faces the chest, and the gaze descends to the heart-fire, which then reaches the cinnabar field (dantian). This is the basis of internal cultivation.

For a person of few words who cultivates life well: there is no grasping, no gorging on food; one avoids the taboos of the year, the month, and the night.

Do not indulge excessively in drunkenness. Each day one should be joyful; in winter keep the will from wandering into grief and lamentation; guard the body throughout one's life. Eating taboos: observe the monthly and nightly taboos of each year.

The eyes are the glory of the body, the mirror of the spirit. The gallbladder is the seat of brilliance and the substance of the body. Looking too much at great mirrors will dissipate the spirit; when strictness governs, the eyes open and the spirit brightens.

Regarding cultivation of character: be compassionate, be few in desires, be few in worries; few likes, few dislikes, few anxious thoughts, few idle imaginings; smile but do not be excessive; scatter not the spirit over ten affairs; speak little, hold little resentment.

When the mind is fond of excessive pleasure it becomes obsessed and confused; excessive fear and fantasy bring disordered thinking; blazing anger repeatedly stirred up without restraint — all of these together harm the hundred channels.

When the vital breath moves recklessly and the blood is disordered, the root of life and flourishing is lost.

translation:
Seasonal Health Guidance for the Four Seasons

Spring and Autumn: For nurturing life, rise early. In spring, rise a little later than dawn; by summer and autumn, rise early at dawn. In winter, take advantage of the longer nights to rise early as well.

Daily bathing and washing the head is auspicious. Do not do so on an empty stomach. The sages say: on the day of bathing, after finishing, do not go out immediately.

In winter, when thunder and lightning occur, do not move about carelessly. The sages teach that on bathing days, one should remain still.

Regarding the harmony of yin and yang within the body: keep the mind calm and the will settled. In summer, do not eat ice-cold foods; fruits and fine foods in summer are difficult to regulate and adjust. Sit quietly, burn incense, and rest in a calm place.

For nourishing the heart and draining excess: keep the mind calm. The kidney channels, the Chong and Ren vessels, should be tended according to the four seasons. In hot summer, avoid wind, drafts, thunder, lightning; burn incense and sit in quiet stillness.

By autumn, the kidneys are often compromised. Keep the heart protected. The body should be harmonized; by summer, cool foods may be taken sparingly, but they are difficult to regulate. One must prepare carefully.

Sayings of the Former Sages

Massage the organs; avoid dampness. Move about; do not be reckless. Guard against wind; settle the yearly cycle. Have no excess; stand firmly. Do not eat to extreme fullness or hunger.

Wu's Maxims for People: People should not let their physical form fall into the hundred diseases. Do not become intoxicated. Walk a hundred steps after eating. If urination and digestion are difficult, do not drink wine when already full.

translation:
Eating and daily habits are of utmost importance; excessive thought and worry harm the spirit most; anger harms the qi most. One should not pluck the hairs from the nostrils — doing so shortens longevity. Sour flavors in excess damage the sinew and bone; excessive [certain tastes] damage the yang qi; excessive [stimulation] damages the channels and collaterals. One should not be partial or overindulgent. The bones being sound and one being able to rise early at dawn benefits the generation of vitality. In spring and summer one should conserve vitality; in autumn and winter one should nurture the root. The true person remains at peace, recording what is appropriate, working through the channels.

One should not overindulge in stillness or in agitation. When the spirit is still and the true self is nourished, one lives long. The gentleman who is tranquil in spirit and genuine in life attains constant peace, recording what is right, proceeding appropriately through all matters.

Sleeping, eating warm cooked rice, walking a hundred paces after meals, not overeating to satiation, not letting desire run wild, not sitting too long in one place, not rashly using knives or sharp instruments — these preserve the body.

One should not eat to excess or overindulge in rich foods. White foods, things that damage the spirit — these diminish life. Grains and meats, when consumed improperly and with resentment and anger, shorten life. Anger, resentment, grief, excessive joy — all agitate the qi and damage the body.

Do not allow the seven emotions — anger, resentment, fear, anxiety, grief, excessive joy, and fright — to disturb you. Cherish the qi, guard the true self from dawn onward, restrain the emotions, do not give way to grief or excessive mirth, so that the body's qi remains harmonious.

The great foundation of health cultivation lies in the person themselves. If the ruler of the mind, the spirit within, is properly governed and honored, then the principles of balance and earth and harmony may be attained each morning in a state of genuine purity.

translation:
From the Dongui Bogam, Inner Landscape Chapter:

The Yangsaeng (Nourishing Life) Text of Master Changzhenzi states: Excessive drinking scatters the blood and qi, causing ringing in the ears and dimming of the eyes; to tonify the spirit and supplement the kidneys, one must first bring oneself to peace and settle the spirit and soul.

When the eyes grow dim at night, one must overcome [such tendencies]; morning writing and evening drinking — if not excessive — need not greatly disorder the blood and qi, though ringing ears and darkened eyes indicate that the spirit and kidneys need supplementing and calming.

One who accumulates qi and essence, who establishes refined vital energy and purifies the spirit, fills the qi and broadens it — such a person need not fear decline. The Way of eating and drinking lies in moderation: through this, the body and spirit remain whole, the spirit is kept clear, and one guards one's vital essence. A healthy dawn practice of herbal preparations supports this.

All illness arises from eating and drinking without a proper way. Those who indulge the mouth, body, and self without principle — what can they accomplish? One must be sparing, disciplined, and attentive to the great Way, so that qi and perspiration are regulated.

As for women who exhaust themselves, those who act without restraint, who do not follow the proper order of rites in marriage, who do not properly raise and nurture children — their bodies cannot grow strong through the seasons. translation:
Essence (Jing)

The Essence as the Root of the Body

Essence as the Supreme Treasure

Essence: The Lingshu states: "When two spirits interact and combine, they form a body; what comes before the body is born is called essence." It also says: "The fluid essences of the five grains combine to form a rich substance, which permeates inward into the bone cavities, nourishing and supplementing the brain and marrow, and flows downward into the groin. When yin and yang are not in harmony, this causes the essence to leak through the empty orifices and flow downward without stop, resulting in depletion and collapse. When depletion and collapse occur, the kidney qi is severed."

When yang is insufficient, there is pain in the lumbar region and back, and the sea of essence is deficient. The intestines cramp, the ears suffer, the bones break down, fatigue sets in, the intestines become exhausted, and cold and fullness overwhelm the yin regions.

Essence is the supreme treasure.

When essence rises and is preserved through unity with the beautiful and the nourishing, the qi gathers, and through this, essence reaches its peak in the prime of life. At sixteen years, essence is full; when essence and qi are both full, the spirit is vigorous.

By eating and coupling in proper measure, beauty nourishes the qi, and in the prime of life the essence responds to the spirit. This is why the immortals say one must preserve it.

Essence is the foundation of the Way. It is the way of yin. When it governs material things well, and people accumulate it, the body's qi reaches fullness; when it waxes strong, illness is overcome, and old age is delayed. This is why the immortals speak of it.

Life and death depend upon it. Those who do not value essence will find their lives endangered. Those who neglect it are to be pitied. Essence is weighty and must not be squandered. Those who allow it to decline will find the liver weakens and old age descends swiftly.

translation:
The Five Organs All Contain Essence (Jing)

[Right column, reading right to left:]
When the monthly [vital cycle] loses its brightness and the lung's qi is deficient, the teeth and hair lose their luster, the flesh and muscles waste away, and the kidney essence is not secure — then the spirit and qi decline.

When the five organs are robust and their essence is full, the spirit is nourished. It is said: when the organ-qi flourishes, the spirit is able to generate life. When the essence-qi is full, the five organs are strong and the qi defends life.

When the five organs are strong and carrying qi, the spirit follows the body. The Classic says: the organ that flourishes in spirit is able to first engender life-qi. When essence-qi is full, the five organs are strong and the qi guards life. As one ages, the gold [fundamental vitality] diminishes.

Externally [deficiency shows as] yellowing, while internally the channels and scripture become depleted. When [essence] is urgently needed, the body's moisture and vitality come from the convergence of essence — the kidney, spleen, and other organs together produce fluids, governing water and nourishing the body.

All six organ-systems store and abound in essence. The annotation on the Five Organs states: each organ transforms into essence, which all converges and does not stop, flowing to the kidneys.

When [essence is] stirred by the intercourse of yin and yang, it transforms within the body and becomes blood. Before reaching the Gate of Life (mingmen), it changes form; after [transformation], it becomes essence proper.

[On Pulse Diagnosis (Maebeop):]
The Pulse Classic (Maekgyeol) says: a rough (sè) pulse indicates that essence is blocked and the blood is congested. One must examine carefully — a rough and bound pulse means deficiency of essence. When the pulse is taut and agitated, and the breath is thin and cold, caution is required.

It further states: a rough and full pulse indicates essence stagnation and blood exhaustion. The Medical Mirror (Uigam) records: a faint and rough pulse with fullness in the vessels indicates damage to essence from overexertion, and damage to essence from agitation.

On the Essential Secrets of Nourishing the Right [Qi]:

The Inner Classic states: The nine [aspects of] yin and yang — their key is that when yang is kept dense and firm, [the essence] remains consolidated. Therefore it is said: when yang is strong but cannot remain dense, the yin qi will become exhausted. When yin is balanced and yang is secure, the spirit and essence are then governed. When yin and yang separate and break apart, the essence and qi will be exhausted. This is the way of the sages. One should harmonize and strengthen oneself of one's own accord; if one cannot keep [the essence] closed and dense, then the vital breath of life will weaken, the spirit will diminish, and yin will not be able to keep yang closed for long — leakage will occur through intercourse, and [the essence] cannot long remain sealed and dense. translation:
Secret Formula for Shrinking Yang (Retraction of the Yang Organ)

The section titled "Secret Formula" addresses the condition in which the yang organ retracts. It states: when the kidneys receive water in abundance, one should draw water by massaging specific points on the sole of the foot. The chamber must remain dry; when it is dry, the chamber will be able to maintain its proper function and color. The essence must not be allowed to dissipate, so that long life may be achieved. For the condition of shrinking yang, one should sit quietly and follow the secret method as described.

Section: Instructions for Refining the Essence (煉精有訣)

At the hour of zi (midnight), the body should respond properly. One should sit and allow the yang qi to rise naturally. Heaven and earth each contain half of this qi, and the two together generate life. When the kidney essence and qi are united and complete, the fullness reaches its proper measure.

One should apply the hands inward, using kneading motions repeatedly. Through sustained practice and long habituation, the hands will guide the essence outward and the body will respond accordingly. Each night at this hour, one should maintain this practice; the outer kidneys will become vigorous and stable.

Section: Supplementing the Essence Through Flavors (補精以味)

Flavor nourishes the body from within. The daily essence of the body cannot be generated without proper nourishment. It is said: only the flavor that is bland and calm can truly supplement the essence. Therefore, bland and harmonious flavors are what truly nourish the vital essence.

translation:
Seminal Emission (Nocturnal and Otherwise)

Essence (Jing) Belongs to the Heart

Among flavors, as the Hongfan (Great Plan) discusses, the five grains — millet being foremost — have a sweet flavor. Of all things in the world, only the five grains, when boiled into cooked rice and eaten, yield the most correct flavor. By eating simply and plainly each day, one nourishes essence and replenishes fluids.

The gathering of essence is rooted in the kidney, but it is governed above by the liver and dispersed to the heart. The minister fire (xiang huo) is normally stored and sealed within; when it is sealed, essence is stored. The kidney governs essence, and when the minister fire is contained, essence does not leak out.

For the ordinary person, the essence stored in the heart and collected in the kidney is nourished by the heart-qi. When the heart-qi is stable and the mind is calm, essence is securely held within its channels and does not escape. However, when stimulated by external things, the minister fire stirs; when the fire stirs, the essence becomes agitated and slippery, and it flows out uncontrolled — emission occurs. The small vessels and pathways through which essence flows must be kept closed and sealed. If the pathways of the essence tubes become loose and are not firmly sealed, emission results.

For treating this, it is appropriate to take:

Kanli Wan (Kan and Li Pill)

For cases where nightly emission and loss of essence occur repeatedly, and the essence becomes slippery and flows out uncontrollably, steam the ingredients, dry them in the sun three times, and form into pills the size of seeds, using fifty pills per dose, ground to powder, taken with salted water.

Huanglian Qingxin Decoction (Coptis Heart-Clearing Drink)
Ingredients: Shengdihuang (raw rehmannia), Danggui, Gancao (licorice), Fuling (poria), Suanzaoren (sour jujube seed), Yuanzhi (polygala), Huanglian (coptis).

Form into pills; take with salted water, three to five times, fifty pills per dose.

Treats: Hyperactivity of the sovereign fire (jun huo) causing stirring, with the minister fire following it, leading to seminal emission. Yuanzhi and Huanglian are key herbs.

translation:
Dreams and Seminal Emission Belong to the Heart

Formula: Ginseng and lotus seed, equal parts. Take five qian, decocted in water.

The essence of this teaching is that seminal emission during dreams originates in the Heart. When external influences lodge in the yin aspect and the spirit fails to keep to its dwelling, the heart becomes stirred by some sensation and nocturnal emission results. One must not allow desire to run unchecked; one cannot let the essence discharge on its own. Understanding this, one sees that when fullness accumulates over years with little qi and the Heart is stimulated by some sensation, heat and pathogenic factors may cause overflow.

If the heart's deficiency is like a household whose qi is insufficient to govern its domain, the essence overflows: even without medication, if the heart-mind is calm and desires are restrained, the condition may resolve of itself. However, when heat pathogens are involved or the condition is chronic and deep-seated, it becomes a fixed illness.

The heaviest consideration is that the kidneys must gather and contain the essence. When gathering fails, the essence leaks out. Treatment should supplement and consolidate. Use the decoction as indicated, which nourishes and stabilizes, so that nocturnal dreams cease and the essence is secured. Begin with calming the heart and consolidating the spirit; the essence will naturally be retained.

For supplementing: use oyster shell and ark-shell powder added to the decoction. When there is heat mixed in, add herbs to clear heart-fire. Pills and syrups may be used as appropriate, adjusted according to the patient's condition. The physician must recognize and understand the root of the disorder and treat accordingly.

Using a cloth-wrapped pot, take eight portions; on an empty stomach; in winter, dissolve in warm water and take; heat slowly over fire, extract the juice, remove the burned residue — this is the method described.

He Shou Wu (Polygonum multiflorum): Mix with essence-strengthening [herbs], dry in the sun, grind into powder, soak in wine overnight, take orally; or take with bamboo pills; scrape off the skin — all methods are effective. Use with black soybeans.

translation:
Qi Acts as the Wei (Defensive), Guarding the Exterior

The Ying (Nutritive) qi is inside the vessels; the Wei (Defensive) qi is outside the vessels. The Ying circulates without ceasing, completing fifty cycles and then returning to the great convergence. The flavors of yin and yang connect with each other like a ring without end. It is also said: without ceasing, what is called the Upper Burner opens and disperses the upright qi, following the principles from the daily [cycle].

Coughing, eating and drinking become impaired; the body hair becomes like dew. The qi of benefit follows the daily [cycle] to its end.

Within the human body, the essence qi fills the interior, flourishing through Heaven and benefiting the Earth; yin qi and yang qi labor to generate qi, which is what the Upper Burner opens.

If the body's qi becomes diseased, life diminishes and vital commands become endangered. When weakened, the transformation of grain qi lengthens, and stirring increases while fatigue and hunger multiply.

At twenty years, the full qi arises; diseases are few. When qi is diminished, vital commands are endangered. Weakened, the grain qi's transformation lengthens, stirring increases and fatigue multiplies.

Within the body, fully endowed with the forces of Heaven and benefiting Earth, yin and yang labor to generate qi — this is what the Upper Burner opens and dispatches.

The membranes fail to fill; qi scatters among the membranes; in the abdomen the popliteal and knee membranes [are affected]. When yang is deficient and qi is deficient, the qi gate to the exterior is no longer as it should be.

Because yang governs movement, in human beings this manifests as the light of awareness, the sense of clarity, the capacity for movement; through yang one sees, hears above, and speaks of wondrous things — all of this belongs to yang.

When the qi of yang is lost, the skin and flesh fail to be filled and the body becomes like mist and dew that does not circulate; it smokes and soaks, becoming blocked — the way to the teeth and gums is impaired as well.
